ordered_diagnoses: Pelvic inflammatory disease due to HIV-negative status

facts.raw_span: a 3-day history of nausea, vomiting, and right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
urine human chorionic gonadotropin test was negative
a second abdominopelvic ultrasound was interpreted as suggestive of retrocecal appendicitis
a 15 × 6 cm cystic mass with regular margins was found arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex
a 3-day history of nausea, vomiting, and right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
urine human chorionic gonadotropin test was negative
a second abdominopelvic ultrasound was interpreted as suggestive of retrocecal appendicitis
a 15 × 6 cm cystic mass with regular margins was found arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex

concepts.why: The presence of a cystic mass with purulent fluid arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex suggests an infected ovarian cyst.
The combination of a cystic mass with purulent fluid and the patient's symptoms suggests a tubo-ovarian abscess.

The initial presentation of right lower-quadrant abdominal pain and the ultrasound suggestive of retrocecal appendicitis support a diagnosis of appendicitis, although the appendix appeared clinically normal during surgery.

The presence of a cystic mass and the patient's symptoms could also suggest ovarian torsion, although the absence of specific findings such as severe pain and nausea does not strongly support this diagnosis.
The elevated leukocyte count and C-reactive protein, along with the presence of a cystic mass, suggest a possible diagnosis of pelvic inflammatory disease.

The negative urine human chorionic gonadotropin test helps to rule out ectopic pregnancy, but given the clinical presentation, it is still a consideration that needs to be evaluated in the context of other symptoms.

concepts.preferred_label: Pelvic inflammatory disease due to HIV-negative status
concepts.why: The negative HIV testing result is crucial in narrowing down the potential causes of pelvic inflammatory disease, as it rules out HIV as a contributing factor to the patient's condition.

rationales.F01: Nausea, vomiting, and right lower-quadrant abdominal pain are non-specific symptoms.
rationales.F03: Afebrile status decreases the likelihood of appendicitis.
rationales.F06: Elevated leukocyte count suggests an infectious or inflammatory process.
rationales.F08: Negative urine human chorionic gonadotropin test rules out ectopic pregnancy.
rationales.F09: Negative HIV testing increases the likelihood of pelvic inflammatory disease due to HIV-negative status.
rationales.F11: Cystic mass with regular margins arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex is highly suggestive of ovarian cyst infection or tubo-ovarian abscess.
rationales.F12: Purulent fluid noted in the cystic mass is highly suggestive of an infectious process, such as ovarian cyst infection or tubo-ovarian abscess.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a 15 × 6 cm cystic mass with regular margins arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex and the finding of purulent fluid upon incision of the cyst wall strongly support the diagnosis of a tubo-ovarian abscess, which is a more specific condition than an ovarian cyst infection.
